Getting started

Design skill

Rules and checks that keep every screen on one style.

Installation

$npx skills add QinYangWang/ui --skill qinyang-design
Download

Or through the shadcn CLI, into .agents/skills:

$pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @qinyang/design-skill

Check

Run it before you commit. It exits with an error when a rule breaks; allow-list a deliberate exception in qinyang-design.config.json with its reason.

node .agents/skills/qinyang-design/scripts/check.mjs
node .agents/skills/qinyang-design/scripts/check.mjs app components --strict
node .agents/skills/qinyang-design/scripts/check.mjs --list

For what only the rendered page shows, open the screen and paste scripts/radius-probe.js (nested corners) or scripts/polish-probe.js (hit areas, image edges, live numbers) into the browser console.

Rules

1.Colour with theme tokens

Tokens follow the theme, the accent preset and dark mode; palette classes and hex values don't.

2.Put text on a solid in its foreground token

The neutral accent's solid is near-white in dark mode, so text-white disappears on it.

3.Fill for state, surface for panels

secondary, muted and accent are translucent fills; anything that floats or holds content needs an opaque surface.

4.Elevate with shadow tokens, not borders plus shadows

Each shadow level already carries its own hairline, so a CSS border on top doubles the edge.

5.Keep series on the chart palette

Eight fixed hues read the same under every accent, in both modes, and keep neighbours apart.

6.Keep nested radii concentric

A child corner that doesn't follow its container's curve reads as a mistake at every radius preset.

7.Stay at or under 16px

Past 16px containers turn into blobs and nested parts can't stay concentric.

8.Derive every radius from the base radius

Presets and the radius slider rescale --radius and the tokens built on it, never literal pixel radii.

Recommendedtsx
<div className="rounded-xl" />
<div className="rounded-[calc(var(--radius)*0.75)]" />
<div className="rounded-[min(calc(var(--radius)*2.8),var(--radius-max))]" />
Avoidtsx
<div className="rounded-[10px]" />
<div style={{ borderRadius: 6 }} />
<div className="rounded-[calc(var(--radius)*2.8)]" />  // passes the cap

9.Use the UI type scale

One compact scale keeps dense screens even; arbitrary sizes drift.

10.Semibold titles, medium labels

Two weights carry the hierarchy; heavier text shouts in a dense layout.

11.Keep the font's tracking

The type is spaced for its size; tightening small text makes it harder to read.

12.Use tabular numbers for numbers that change or align

Proportional digits make columns and counters jump.

13.Size controls for desktop density

Desktop screens hold more per view; touch-sized controls waste it.

14.Space related things closer

Spacing groups content before any border does.

15.Start navigation text on one left edge

Indents and guide lines widen the sidebar and break the column the eye follows.

16.Compose the library, don't restyle it

A component's variants and sizes are its design; overriding them per screen forks the style.

Recommendedtsx
<Button variant="outline" size="sm">Export</Button>
<Button className="w-full">Continue</Button>   // layout only
Avoidtsx
<Button className="h-10 rounded-full px-6 font-bold shadow-lg">
  Export
</Button>

17.Keep a menu label inside its group

The label names the group for assistive tech, and the primitive label throws outside one.

Recommendedtsx
<MenuContent>
  <MenuGroup>
    <MenuLabel>Agent</MenuLabel>
    <MenuItem>Code reviewer</MenuItem>
    <MenuItem>Release notes</MenuItem>
  </MenuGroup>
</MenuContent>
Avoidtsx
<MenuContent>
  <MenuLabel>Agent</MenuLabel>
  <MenuItem>Code reviewer</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem>Release notes</MenuItem>
</MenuContent>

18.Chevrons for folders, file icons for files

A folder icon next to a chevron says the same thing twice and pushes names apart.

19.Draw icons from one family per group

Two glyph families in one group look like two different products.

20.Frame title icons, keep nav icons bare

A frame marks an icon as the subject of a card; in a list it is clutter.

21.Use real brand marks for other products

Redrawn or approximated logos look wrong to anyone who knows the brand.

22.Show people and workspaces as avatars

An avatar says "who"; a generic icon in that spot says nothing.

23.Answer a press with a fill

Native controls don't shrink when pressed; scaling every button makes the screen feel springy.

24.Transition named properties, briefly

transition-all animates layout you didn't mean to, and slow hovers feel laggy.

Recommendedtsx
<div className="transition-[box-shadow,background-color] duration-150 ease-out hover:bg-secondary" />
<Panel className="transition-[opacity,translate] duration-300" />
Avoidtsx
<div className="transition-all duration-500 hover:bg-secondary" />

25.Gate movement on reduced motion

Movement, scale and blur can make some readers ill; an opacity fade carries the same change.

Recommendedtsx
const reduce = useReducedMotion()
<motion.div
  initial={reduce ? { opacity: 0 } : { opacity: 0, y: 12, filter: "blur(4px)" }}
  animate={{ opacity: 1, y: 0, filter: "blur(0px)" }}
/>
Avoidtsx
<motion.div initial={{ opacity: 0, y: 40, scale: 0.8 }} animate={{ opacity: 1, y: 0, scale: 1 }} />

26.Show a ring on keyboard focus

Keyboard users need to see where they are; a hover style doesn't help them.

27.Let the preview explain

A live preview already shows the look, layout and states; text that repeats it is noise.

28.Keep descriptions to one plain sentence

A registry description is the page lede, the search text and the meta tag at once.

29.Never write colon lists or stacked adjectives

"X: a, b, c and d" and "powerful, seamless" read as filler.

30.Describe what it does, not where it came from

Copy names the job, not the projects behind it.

31.Name template parts apart from registry items

A part file named like an item (parts/avatar.tsx next to the avatar item) collides on install and in imports.

Recommendedtext
components/blog/parts/author-avatar.tsx
components/vscode/parts/buffers.ts
Avoidtext
components/blog/parts/avatar.tsx     # same name as @qinyang/avatar
components/vscode/parts/docs.ts       # same name as @qinyang/docs

32.Run the upgrade check after a theme update

The CLI adds and updates theme variables but never deletes one, so removed tokens linger.

Recommendedbash
npx shadcn@latest add @qinyang/theme --overwrite
npx shadcn@latest add @qinyang/upgrade-check
node scripts/qinyang-upgrade-check.mjs --fix
Avoidbash
npx shadcn@latest add @qinyang/theme --overwrite
# removed tokens stay in globals.css

33.Give every target 24px to land on

A 16px checkbox or close button is hard to hit with a trackpad and harder with a finger.

Recommendedtsx
// A 16px close button keeps its look and reaches 24px through a pseudo-element.
import { XIcon } from "@/components/icons"

export function ChipClose({ onClose }: { onClose: () => void }) {
  return (
    <button
      type="button"
      aria-label="Remove"
      onClick={onClose}
      className="relative grid size-4 place-items-center rounded-sm text-muted-foreground after:absolute after:-inset-1 hover:text-foreground pointer-coarse:after:-inset-3.5"
    >
      <XIcon className="size-3" />
    </button>
  )
}
Avoidtsx
// 16px is all there is to hit; on a trackpad it takes two tries.
import { XIcon } from "@/components/icons"

export function ChipClose({ onClose }: { onClose: () => void }) {
  return (
    <button type="button" aria-label="Remove" onClick={onClose} className="grid size-4 place-items-center rounded-sm text-muted-foreground hover:text-foreground">
      <XIcon className="size-3" />
    </button>
  )
}

34.Trim the icon side of a button

An icon's side bearing adds space, so equal padding pushes the content off centre.

Recommendedtsx
import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button"
import { PlusIcon } from "@/components/icons"

// data-icon trims 2px on the icon side, so the content looks centred.
export function NewButton() {
  return (
    <Button>
      <PlusIcon data-icon="inline-start" />
      New project
    </Button>
  )
}
Avoidtsx
import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button"
import { PlusIcon } from "@/components/icons"

// Equal padding: the icon's side bearing makes the start look wider than the end.
export function NewButton() {
  return (
    <Button>
      <PlusIcon />
      New project
    </Button>
  )
}

35.Outline images with a neutral hairline

Without an edge a pale photo melts into a white card; a grey border picks up the surface tint.

Recommendedtsx
// A neutral inset hairline keeps a light photo's edge on a white card.
export function Cover({ src, alt }: { src: string; alt: string }) {
  return <img src={src} alt={alt} className="aspect-video w-full rounded-lg object-cover media-outline" />
}
Avoidtsx
// No edge: a pale image melts into the surface behind it.
export function Cover({ src, alt }: { src: string; alt: string }) {
  return <img src={src} alt={alt} className="aspect-video w-full rounded-lg object-cover" />
}

36.Cross-fade icon swaps

A glyph that cuts from copy to check is easy to miss; one that changes in place reads as a new state.

Recommendedtsx
import { AnimatePresence, motion } from "motion/react"

import { CheckIcon, CopyIcon } from "@/components/icons"
import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button"

// The glyph changes in place: scale 0.25, blur 4px and opacity 0 on the way in and out.
// With the action-swap-blur item installed, <ActionSwapBlurIcon value={…}> does the same.
const hidden = { opacity: 0, scale: 0.25, filter: "blur(4px)" }

export function CopyButton({ copied, onCopy }: { copied: boolean; onCopy: () => void }) {
  return (
    <Button variant="ghost" size="icon-sm" aria-label={copied ? "Copied" : "Copy"} onClick={onCopy}>
      <AnimatePresence initial={false} mode="popLayout">
        <motion.span
          key={copied ? "copied" : "copy"}
          initial={hidden}
          animate={{ opacity: 1, scale: 1, filter: "blur(0px)" }}
          exit={hidden}
          transition={{ type: "spring", duration: 0.3, bounce: 0 }}
          className="inline-flex"
        >
          {copied ? <CheckIcon /> : <CopyIcon />}
        </motion.span>
      </AnimatePresence>
    </Button>
  )
}
Avoidtsx
import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button"
import { CheckIcon, CopyIcon } from "@/components/icons"

// The glyph cuts from copy to check, so the change is easy to miss.
export function CopyButton({ copied, onCopy }: { copied: boolean; onCopy: () => void }) {
  return (
    <Button variant="ghost" size="icon-sm" aria-label={copied ? "Copied" : "Copy"} onClick={onCopy}>
      {copied ? <CheckIcon /> : <CopyIcon />}
    </Button>
  )
}

37.Transition states, keyframe one-offs

A transition retargets when a state flips mid-way; a keyframe restarts and snaps.

Recommendedtsx
// Open and closed are two states of one transition, so a quick toggle reverses smoothly.
export function Reveal({ open, children }: { open: boolean; children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <div data-open={open || undefined} className="opacity-0 transition-[opacity,translate] duration-200 ease-[cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1)] data-open:translate-y-0 data-open:opacity-100 motion-safe:translate-y-1">
      {children}
    </div>
  )
}
Avoidtsx
// A keyframe restarts from frame one when the state flips mid-way, so a quick toggle snaps.
export function Reveal({ open, children }: { open: boolean; children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <div data-open={open || undefined} className="opacity-0 data-open:animate-[fade-up_200ms_ease-out_forwards]">
      {children}
    </div>
  )
}

38.Leave quieter than you arrive

The eye has moved on to what comes next; a big exit pulls it back.

Recommendedtsx
import { motion } from "motion/react"

// The toast leaves with a short rise and a fade, faster than it came in.
export function Toast({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <motion.div
      initial={{ opacity: 0, y: 12, filter: "blur(4px)" }}
      animate={{ opacity: 1, y: 0, filter: "blur(0px)" }}
      exit={{ opacity: 0, y: -12, filter: "blur(4px)", transition: { duration: 0.15 } }}
      className="rounded-xl bg-popover p-3 shadow-surface"
    >
      {children}
    </motion.div>
  )
}
Avoidtsx
import { motion } from "motion/react"

// Shrinking to half size and flying a full height pulls the eye back to something that is leaving.
export function Toast({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <motion.div initial={{ opacity: 0 }} animate={{ opacity: 1 }} exit={{ opacity: 0, y: "-100%", scale: 0.5 }} className="rounded-xl bg-popover p-3 shadow-surface">
      {children}
    </motion.div>
  )
}

39.Recolour icons with CSS, keep their stroke and grid

A thicker stroke, an off-grid size or a baked-in fill makes one glyph look like another set.

Recommendedtsx
// One SVG painted with currentColor; hover and selected states are text colours.
export function Dot() {
  return (
    <svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" className="size-4 text-muted-foreground hover:text-foreground aria-selected:text-primary">
      <circle cx="8" cy="8" r="4" fill="currentColor" />
    </svg>
  )
}
Avoidtsx
// A baked-in colour can't follow hover, selection, dark mode or the accent.
export function Dot() {
  return (
    <svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" className="size-4">
      <circle cx="8" cy="8" r="4" fill="#0090ff" />
    </svg>
  )
}

40.Name every icon-only button

A screen reader announces an unnamed icon button as "button" and nothing else.

Recommendedtsx
import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button"
import { TrashIcon } from "@/components/icons"

// The name a screen reader announces, and the text its tooltip shows.
export function DeleteButton({ onDelete }: { onDelete: () => void }) {
  return (
    <Button variant="ghost" size="icon-sm" aria-label="Delete" onClick={onDelete}>
      <TrashIcon />
    </Button>
  )
}
Avoidtsx
import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button"
import { TrashIcon } from "@/components/icons"

// Announced as "button" and nothing else.
export function DeleteButton({ onDelete }: { onDelete: () => void }) {
  return (
    <Button variant="ghost" size="icon-sm" onClick={onDelete}>
      <TrashIcon />
    </Button>
  )
}
